summary: 新末起兵、昆阳破新，重建汉室而定都洛阳，以柔道治国、封禅告成的中兴开国皇帝。

bio_md:
# 汉光武帝 · 主要事迹

刘秀是新末乱世中重建汉室的中兴之主。本页以《后汉书·光武帝纪》为年表主线，辅以云台诸将与马援诸传互见。

新莽地皇三年（22），他随宗室宾客起兵于舂陵，卷入反新浪潮；次年昆阳之战以少击众，大破[[xin-wang-mang|王莽]]新军主力，一举奠定军事声望。更始年间，他渡河经营河北，收揽人才，与更始政权渐行渐远；建武元年（25）于鄗南即皇帝位，建元建武，国号续汉，随即定都洛阳，东汉政治中心由此确立。

建国之后，他一面收束武功，一面塑造政风。建武二年大封功臣，云台班底成形；建武十二年平公孙述等，全国粗定，中兴局面落定；建武十九年，马援等平交趾，武功延伸至南疆。文治一面，他崇尚柔道、退功臣进文吏，不使功臣揽政；建武十五年推行度田，检核田亩户口，曾引发地方反抗与政策调整，成为其治世中争议最集中的节点。

晚年，他于中元元年（56）封禅泰山，中兴礼仪达于高峰，可与[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]的封禅对读：一人把统一帝国的武功与礼仪推向极盛，一人在废墟之后以此告成功于天地。翌年（中元二年，57）他崩于洛阳，明帝继位，东汉国祚得以延续。史家评点多聚焦于「柔道」与度田之争，总体月旦正面。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Xiu was the restoration sovereign who rebuilt the Han house amid the chaos at the end of the Xin dynasty. This page takes the 《后汉书·光武帝纪》 as its chronological backbone, cross-referenced with the biographies of the Yuntai generals and of Ma Yuan.

In Dihuang 3 of the Xin (22), he rose in arms at Chongling with imperial kinsmen and retainers, joining the tide of revolt against the Xin; the next year, at the Battle of Kunyang, he struck the many with the few and shattered the main Xin army of

, establishing his military renown in a single stroke. During the Gengshi period he crossed the river to build a base in Hebei, gathering talent and drifting steadily away from the Gengshi regime; in Jianwu 1 (25) he took the imperial throne south of Hao, founded the Jianwu era, continued the Han dynastic name, and soon fixed the capital at Luoyang, thereby establishing the political center of the Eastern Han.

Once the state was founded, he wound down military ventures while shaping the political climate. In Jianwu 2 he broadly enfeoffed meritorious officials, and the Yuntai cohort took shape; in Jianwu 12 he defeated Gongsun Shu and other rivals, the realm was roughly pacified, and the restoration settled into place; in Jianwu 19 Ma Yuan and others pacified Jiaozhi, extending the martial record to the southern frontier. On the civil side, he prized the "way of softness," retired meritorious generals in favor of civil officials, and kept the generals from holding power; in Jianwu 15 he pushed through the land survey, auditing fields and households, which provoked local resistance and policy adjustments — the most contested node of his rule.

In his later years, in Zhongyuan 1 (56), he performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices at Mount Tai, the ritual high point of the restoration, which can be read against the Feng-Shan of

: one carried the unified empire's martial and ritual order to its zenith, the other used the same rites to announce to Heaven and Earth that success had been won from ruins. The following year (Zhongyuan 2, 57) he died at Luoyang; Emperor Ming succeeded him, and the Eastern Han dynastic line was preserved. Historians' verdicts focus on the "way of softness" and the land-survey controversy, and are on the whole favorable.
